arc_assessment: The sequence keeps its promise. The cover's range and its one number get paid on 02, the admission on 05 is a real turn, the dates on 07 complicate it, and 09 lands the one ask on the same 2 to 16 the deck opened with. The middle stumbles twice. 03 swaps dens for bears ('median, 4' straight after 'FWS estimates 8') with nothing printed to bridge the change of unit. 04's 12 is only ever 10 + 2 in the reader's head. And 05 through 08 are four text-heavy frames in a row, so the felt escalation flattens before the close.

junction_pulls.pull: The gold 8 sitting inside a bracket eight times wider ('why 8?'). The identical rail on 02 confirms it is the same object.
Nothing on 02 plants 'and in bears?'. The swipe rides on the rail alone, and 03 opens on a number (4) that seems to contradict the 8.
The gold caps 10 and 2 become the gold 12 on 04, but the sum is never printed. A skimmer sees '12' with no link back to 03.
The rail coming back with its 8 to 16 half gone to phantom dashes is clever but tiny. 04 plants no doubt for 05 to pay.
The admission makes the reader ask 'so what checks it?', and 06's kicker 'BEFORE ANY SEISMIC LINE' answers. It is implicit but it works.
'Two infrared surveys' invites 'when?', and 07's headline pays it hard ('last winter's dates').
The 2026 slabs sit past December 17th, but 'IF AUTHORIZED' is only reached by turning the page. No element on 07 points at the machines.
'A decision isn't expected until mid-January' hands off to 'COMMENTS CLOSE DECEMBER 17TH'. A clear deadline pull.

continuity_findings.problem: The deck header promises that 03's lit ledge runs off right into 04's slab. 04's slab sits on a near-black void with no ledge plane, so the tease never completes.
continuity_findings.fix: Carry 03's lit ledge top plane (same tone and height band) under 04's slab as the ground it casts onto. That also lifts 04's mean toward its declared peak.

continuity_findings.problem: The header says 08's node line leaves the right edge. It leaves lower left and continues into nothing on 09.
continuity_findings.fix: Fix the header text, or angle the node line to exit right toward 09's dunes.

continuity_findings.problem: The state table says 0 to 2 km. The build ships 0 to 5 km, which is reconciled and correct: the 1.6 mark at 370 display px from 0 matches the ring radius. The labels skip '1', so the gold 1.6 floats between unlabeled ticks.
continuity_findings.fix: Label ticks 1, 2 and 4, or keep 0, 1.6 and 5 with the minor ticks shorter.

rhythm_findings.problem: Four word-heavy frames in a row: a 29-word quote at 58 px, then 37, 29 and 38-word bodies, each with a chart or object beneath. 06, 07 and 08 alone are three dense slides in a row, which breaks the alternation rule. The only breather (04) comes before the stretch where fatigue actually sets in.
rhythm_findings.fix: Cut 08 to the headline plus one line ('37,500 nodes. Up to $175.0 million.'), move the Beacon mid-January line into the caption, and let the vehicle frame breathe. Optionally trim 06's body to two sentences (keep the twice-flown survey and the 1.6 km zone, drop SnowDens/FLIR to the caption).

rhythm_findings.problem: 02 and 03 are both headline plus 30 to 40 word body plus art. 03 also adds a two-line mono note, which makes it the densest frame in the deck.
rhythm_findings.fix: Move the nonlethal/0.15 note to the caption or shrink it to one line.

consistency_findings.problem: This frame looks pasted from another deck. Pale desaturated grey snow with no aurora tint, toy-primitive vehicles, and the brightest field in the sequence (census L* 28 against 04's 25). Every other frame lives in night navy with aurora-green light.
consistency_findings.fix: Re-expose 08 to the night palette (snow lee #23384A to lit #BFD8D4, aurora-green rim from upper left) so the headlight pools are the only bright ground. Target mean L* around 18.

consistency_findings.problem: 'A YEAR EARLIER' is cut by the gold December 17th line through 'YEAR', and 'PROPOSED TERMS, AS LISTED' overlaps the phantom slabs' dashes. The phantom 2025 slabs also float above their rail rather than standing on it.
consistency_findings.fix: Move 'A YEAR EARLIER' right of the gold tick or onto the dotted span's midpoint, start the row label after the phantom slabs, and seat the phantoms on the rail top.

consistency_findings.problem: Transcription. Counters read ALASKA.AI 01/09, 02/09, 03/09, 04/09, 05/09, 06/09, 07/09, 08/09, 09/09, all correct. Kicker at top left, counter at top right, alaskaaihq.com at bottom left, and the rail trough at the same y on all nine. Gold carries a single meaning, absent on 08 as planned. Rail data verified: 03 bars end at 14 and 11, stakes at 10 and 2; 07 gold tick lands on December 17th, 2026 (x 1286 display = day 411 of 457); 08 shows twelve vermilion ticks.

predicted_bail_point.why: The cover and 02 drill in '8 dens'. 03's headline then says 'Den model median, 4', and the only bridge is the small mono kicker 'IN BEARS A WINTER'. A skimmer reads that as a contradiction, and 03 is also the densest frame (headline, 34-word body, 2-line note, two-row chart). A reader who got through 3 slides would likely finish, but the ones who bail do it here or at 06, the third straight text wall.
predicted_bail_point.fix: Put the change of unit in the headline, e.g. 'In bears disturbed: a median of 4. Proposed cap, 10.' (C12, C15, already on the slide), and drop the mono note to the caption.

weakest_frames.problem: The largest object, the hero vibroseis, is the least modelled in the deck: untextured rounded boxes, tracks as black blobs with no road wheels or lugs, no visible baseplate or mast, and a vermilion stripe that dithers into streaks. The cab side glass carries a garbled pixel-noise texture at about (1030, 1090) display, a cause d artifact as well. The 'eleven distant vehicles' are a near conga line of identical clones, larger than the hero's own scale cue, with no fog. There are no raking headlight cones, and the lower third is flat over-exposed grey snow with a blown smudge at lower right.
weakest_frames.fix: Rebuild the hero at real detail and light it as night: track modules with road wheels and lugged tread, the baseplate and mast visible between the tracks, a fixed glass material, the ground exposure dropped so two headlight cones are the only lit snow, and the eleven others pushed back into fog.

weakest_frames.problem: The calendar occupies a thin band and the slabs are tiny cubes. The lower third (y 1500 to 1750 display) is a near-empty pool of scattered dash hachures that reads as placeholder. Labels collide (see consistency findings).
weakest_frames.fix: Scale the calendar to fill y 1000 to 1750: taller row rails and slabs about twice the size. Replace the dash pool with a modelled lit snow strip that catches the slabs' casts.

weakest_frames.problem: The snow plain is horizontal streak lines that read as a scanline/banding artifact rather than wind ripples. The aurora is a small right-side patch whose base edge glows like a lit hill outline. The left half between the attribution and the horizon (about y 1100 to 1450) is dead.
weakest_frames.fix: Widen the curtain into a low arc across the full horizon behind the ridge, at three depths, and replace the streak plain with the planned graded green sheen plus short ripple hachures lit on their aurora-facing sides.

weakest_frames.problem: The slab reads as perforated metal pegboard, not pressed snow: rigid machine-even hollows with no grain variation in the rims. The band between body and slab (about y 650 to 900) is empty, and the ground cast is barely visible on near-black, which is also why this declared peak measures below 08.
weakest_frames.fix: Seat the slab on a lit snow ground (03's ledge tone) with a visible soft cast, and give each hollow a softened, slightly irregular snow rim.

weakest_frames.problem: The micro-normal sastrugi texture added in fix round 1 reads as fur or moire at zoom on the lower-right lit faces. The planned masterful-depth devices (tack-sharp lit crest, blurred foreground drift lip, one hero ridge) are not there, so the field is an even ripple sheet. The mid band between the subhead and the horizon is empty sky.
weakest_frames.fix: Halve the micro-normal frequency and amplitude, and add the blurred repoussoir drift lip at lower left against one sharp lit crest as the focal point.

weakest_frames.problem: The aurora is rendered as a regular vertical comb of stripes. The same fur-like micro-ripple moire runs across the lower-right snow. A dark blurred smudge sits under the site fixture at lower left, and the wordmark floats on a dead trough.
weakest_frames.fix: Break the aurora ray spacing with noise-modulated widths and alpha (no fixed pitch), and reduce the snow micro-normal as on 01.

cross_frame.problem: The fix-round micro-normal snow is the same texture on three frames, at the reuse limit rather than over it. On 01 and 09 it resolves as fur or moire at zoom, so the shared texture is also a shared artifact.
cross_frame.fix: Lower its frequency and give each frame its own scale and orientation: wind-aligned on 01, dune-aligned on 09, and smooth under headlights on 08.

cross_frame.problem: Tonal census: 01 17, 02 15, 03 20, 04 25, 05 8, 06 14, 07 11, 08 28, 09 21, against a declared peak on 04 and darkest frame on 05. The WARN is the miss I see. 08's over-exposed grey snow is the lit frame of the deck, so the brightest moment belongs to the machines, not the breather, and the frame reads off-palette. 05 does land as the darkest. 06 and 07 sit dark when mid-tone was planned, so the middle sags.
cross_frame.fix: Bring 08 down to about L* 18 with night-tinted snow, and lift 04 to about L* 30 by giving the slab a lit ground plane.

cross_frame.problem: REUSE census: AKPOST.field on 01, 05, 06 and 09. On the sheet these are a heightfield, ray-base curves, Tanaka contours and dunes, so it does not read as the same drawing.
